paragraphs: Children in care in Southampton are looked after by Southampton City Council's own fostering service, alongside the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. The council's aim is to give local children a safe and caring foster home close to where they already live, and it looks for carers for children of every age, from newborn babies to teenagers.

The council offers several kinds of fostering, including respite breaks, short-term care while a longer plan is agreed, long-term fostering, parent and child placements, emergency placements, supported lodgings for young people aged 16 to 21, step-across care for young people moving from a children's home into a family, and care for unaccompanied children seeking asylum. New carers are usually encouraged to begin with short-term fostering.

Each carer has a dedicated supervising social worker, and there is round-the-clock help from the Emergency Duty Team, along with support groups, social events and the Mockingbird programme. Carers can join the Southampton Foster Carers Association and FosterTalk. Training includes mandatory courses such as First Aid and Record Keeping, then core and specialist sessions on subjects like attachment, trauma and life story work. The council's published rates for 2026/27 give a weekly maintenance allowance from £190 for children aged 0 to 2 up to £288 for young people aged 16 and over (after a small weekly amount is set aside as savings for the child), plus a weekly skills fee per child of £120, £240 or £350 depending on the carer's level.

Becoming a carer starts with initial checks, which generally take around two months, followed by a Form F assessment, usually completed within four months, before an approval panel. Anyone over 21 can apply. A good next step is to speak to the council and to two or three of the agencies listed below, comparing the training, support and pay each one offers.
